data.shortName: AU Mandatory Guardrails for AI - Consultation
data.fullName: Mandatory Guardrails for AI in High-Risk Settings — Proposals Paper
data.summary: Government consultation on mandatory guardrails for AI used in high-risk settings (health, employment, credit, law enforcement). Proposes a risk-based framework requiring testing, transparency, human oversight, and accountability for AI systems that significantly affect individuals' rights. Builds on the Voluntary AI Safety Standard.
data.whyItMatters: If DocuSign uses AI for document processing, identity verification, or risk assessment in these high-risk domains, mandatory guardrails would apply directly. Even if not high-risk, the framework signals where AU AI regulation is heading.
data.complianceImplications: Review AI features against proposed high-risk definitions. Prepare AI risk assessments and documentation. Consider participating in the consultation to influence scope.
data.penalties: TBD — consultation stage. Expected to include administrative penalties.
data.regulator: Department of Industry, Science and Resources

data.shortName: AU Privacy Act - Children's Online Privacy Code Development
data.fullName: Privacy Act — Children's Online Privacy Code Development Consultation
data.summary: The OAIC is developing the Children's Online Privacy Code under the Tranche 1 reforms. Consultation on the scope, design principles, and obligations for services likely accessed by children. Expected to impose age-appropriate design requirements on digital services.
data.whyItMatters: Even B2B platforms may be captured if they're 'likely to be accessed by children.' The Code's scope is still being defined and could be broad. Early engagement is important.
data.complianceImplications: Monitor scope definition. If captured, would need to implement age-appropriate privacy protections, data minimization for minors, and potentially age assurance mechanisms.
data.penalties: OAIC enforcement powers under Privacy Act — civil penalty provisions
data.regulator: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

data.shortName: AU Cyber Security Act 2024
data.fullName: Cyber Security Act 2024
data.summary: Australia's first standalone cybersecurity legislation, passed November 2024. Introduces mandatory ransomware payment reporting for businesses with A$3M+ turnover (within 72 hours), security standards for smart devices, a Cyber Incident Review Board, and a limited-use framework for information shared with the Australian Signals Directorate during incidents.
data.whyItMatters: DocuSign would need to report any ransomware payment to the Australian Signals Directorate within 72 hours. The limited-use framework encourages sharing incident information with government without fear of regulatory action based on that information.
data.complianceImplications: Implement ransomware payment reporting procedures. Assess smart device security standards if applicable. Leverage the limited-use safe harbor for incident information sharing with ASD.
data.penalties: Failure to report ransomware payments: civil penalties up to 60 penalty units (A$18,780). Smart device security: TBD in standards.
data.regulator: Department of Home Affairs / Australian Signals Directorate

data.shortName: AU Digital ID Act Expansion
data.fullName: Digital ID Act 2024 — Expansion to Private Sector
data.summary: The Digital ID Act 2024 established the Australian Government Digital ID System with an accreditation framework. The government is consulting on expanding the scheme to allow private sector organizations to become accredited identity providers and relying parties. Would enable standardized digital identity verification across government and private sector.
data.whyItMatters: Direct opportunity for DocuSign's identity verification and Identify product. If the digital ID framework expands to private sector, DocuSign could integrate with accredited digital IDs for high-assurance signer verification in Australia.
data.complianceImplications: Monitor expansion to private sector. Consider accreditation as a relying party. Integrate with Australian digital ID standards for identity verification features.
data.penalties: Accreditation framework — non-compliance with accreditation rules, not criminal penalties

data.shortName: SG Generative AI Model Governance Framework
data.fullName: Proposed Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI
data.summary: IMDA and AI Verify Foundation are developing a governance framework specifically for generative AI, building on the existing Model AI Governance Framework. Addresses hallucination risks, content provenance, copyright concerns, and responsible deployment. Discussion paper released for industry consultation.
data.whyItMatters: If DocuSign deploys generative AI features (contract drafting, clause generation, document summarization) in Singapore, this framework will set expectations. Singapore's frameworks often become de facto regional standards.
data.complianceImplications: Align any generative AI features with the framework's principles. Implement content provenance and transparency measures. Address hallucination risks in AI-generated legal content.
data.penalties: Non-binding — but voluntary compliance expected. May inform future regulation.

data.shortName: SG PDPA Advisory Guidelines on AI
data.fullName: PDPC Advisory Guidelines on Use of Personal Data in AI Recommendation and Decision Systems
data.summary: Updated advisory guidelines from the PDPC addressing how the PDPA applies to AI systems that use personal data for recommendations and decisions. Covers consent for AI training data, notification requirements, data protection impact assessments for AI, and accountability for automated decisions.
data.whyItMatters: Directly applicable if DocuSign uses AI/ML to process personal data of Singapore individuals — whether for document recommendations, risk scoring, or identity verification.
data.complianceImplications: Review AI data processing against updated guidelines. Ensure consent covers AI/ML use of personal data. Conduct DPIAs for AI features processing Singapore personal data.
data.penalties: PDPA penalties apply — up to S$1 million or 10% of annual turnover

data.shortName: SG MLETR Implementation — Trade Documents
data.fullName: UNCITRAL MLETR Implementation — Electronic Transferable Records for Trade
data.summary: Singapore adopted MLETR through the 2021 ETA amendments, enabling electronic bills of lading, promissory notes, and other transferable records. IMDA is working with industry to develop standards and use cases for electronic transferable records in trade finance.
data.whyItMatters: Major growth opportunity for DocuSign. Electronic bills of lading and trade documents represent a significant TAM. Singapore is positioning as a global hub for digital trade documents.
data.complianceImplications: Monitor standards development. Position DocuSign's platform for electronic transferable record use cases. Engage with IMDA's industry working groups.
data.penalties: N/A — enabling framework

data.shortName: JP APPI Amendment Bill 2026
data.fullName: Act on Protection of Personal Information — Amendment Bill 2026
data.summary: Major amendment bill submitted to the Diet introducing GDPR-style administrative fines (kacho-kin), streamlined breach reporting requirements, potential reclassification of biometric data as sensitive personal information, strengthened protections for minors, and new rules on automated decision-making. The most significant reform since the 2020 amendment.
data.whyItMatters: Administrative fines would dramatically increase DocuSign's compliance risk in Japan. Biometric data reclassification could affect identity verification features. Automated decision-making rules may apply to AI-powered contract analysis.
data.complianceImplications: Budget for significant compliance uplift. Review identity verification features for biometric data handling. Prepare for administrative fine regime. Assess automated decision-making features against new rules.
data.penalties: Proposed administrative fines — quantum under deliberation but expected to be proportional to revenue, similar to GDPR

data.shortName: JP Digital Agency — Hanko Reform Roadmap
data.fullName: Digital Agency Roadmap for Administrative Procedure Digitization (Hanko Reform)
data.summary: The Digital Agency continues to drive elimination of hanko (seal) requirements across government and private sector procedures. The roadmap targets removing stamp requirements from all national government procedures by 2025, with ongoing work to encourage private sector adoption of electronic signatures.
data.whyItMatters: Each hanko requirement that gets removed is a new use case for DocuSign. The Digital Agency's push is the single biggest market tailwind for e-signatures in Japan. Private sector adoption is accelerating.
data.complianceImplications: Track hanko removal progress across government agencies and industries. Align product features and marketing with newly digitized procedures. Partner with Digital Agency initiatives where possible.
data.penalties: N/A — policy initiative

keyDates.label: Target: all national government hanko requirements removed

data.shortName: JP Economic Security — Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity
data.fullName: Economic Security Promotion Act — Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity Regulations
data.summary: Regulations under the Economic Security Promotion Act requiring advance screening of critical software and equipment used in essential infrastructure. Cloud services used by designated critical infrastructure operators may require government pre-approval. Supply chain security requirements being phased in.
data.whyItMatters: If DocuSign's platform is classified as critical software used by Japanese essential infrastructure operators (finance, telecommunications, etc.), it could be subject to government screening. Supply chain requirements may affect how DocuSign procures and deploys infrastructure in Japan.
data.complianceImplications: Monitor designated critical infrastructure definitions. Assess whether DocuSign's services are used by designated operators. Prepare for potential government screening of cloud platforms.
data.penalties: Non-compliance with screening requirements could result in usage prohibition for designated infrastructure

data.shortName: IN Digital India Act (Proposed)
data.fullName: Digital India Act (Proposed)
data.summary: Proposed comprehensive digital legislation to replace the Information Technology Act 2000. Expected to modernize the legal framework for online platforms, intermediary liability, digital competition, user safety, and emerging technologies. Multiple rounds of consultation completed. Would overhaul the e-signature and electronic records framework.
data.whyItMatters: Would fundamentally reshape the legal basis for electronic signatures and digital transactions in India. The current IT Act 2000 is DocuSign's primary enabling legislation — its replacement could change compliance requirements significantly.
data.complianceImplications: Monitor closely — this would replace the IT Act that underpins DocuSign's legal validity in India. Engage with consultations to ensure e-signature provisions remain favorable. Prepare for potential new intermediary obligations.
data.penalties: TBD — expected to introduce graduated penalty framework

keyDates.label: Bill expected to be introduced in Parliament

data.regulator: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

data.shortName: IN DPDP Rules 2025
data.fullName: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
data.summary: Implementing rules for the DPDP Act 2023, notified on 13 November 2025 with phased commencement. Specify detailed requirements for consent mechanisms, notice formats, data principal rights procedures, breach notification timelines, Significant Data Fiduciary obligations, Data Protection Board procedures, and consent manager registration.
data.whyItMatters: The Rules make the DPDP Act operational. They specify exactly what DocuSign must do — consent notice format, breach notification timelines (72 hours to Board), verification procedures for data principal rights, and how to handle cross-border transfers.
data.complianceImplications: Implement consent notices in prescribed format. Build data principal rights request workflows with prescribed timelines. Establish 72-hour breach notification to DPBI. Assess if Significant Data Fiduciary designation applies. Register as consent manager if applicable.
data.penalties: Same as DPDP Act — up to INR 250 crore. Rules specify procedural compliance that triggers Act penalties.

keyDates.label: Phase 1: Board setup and basic provisions
Phase 2: Consent managers and Board inquiry powers

data.shortName: IN Corporate Laws Amendment Bill 2026
data.fullName: Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026
data.summary: Proposes amendments to the Companies Act 2013 including fully virtual AGMs/EGMs, mandatory company websites, simplified cross-border mergers, and enhanced digital governance requirements. Referred to Joint Parliamentary Committee for examination in April 2026.
data.whyItMatters: Virtual AGMs and mandatory digital governance create direct demand for DocuSign's platform. If enacted, every Indian company above a certain size would need digital infrastructure for corporate governance — a significant market opportunity.
data.complianceImplications: Position DocuSign for virtual AGM/EGM market. Ensure platform supports Indian corporate governance requirements for digital meetings and electronic voting.
data.penalties: Companies Act penalty framework applies

data.shortName: HK PDPO Reform — Mandatory Breach Notification
data.fullName: Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance Reform — Mandatory Data Breach Notification and Administrative Fines
data.summary: The PCPD has been advocating for mandatory data breach notification and the introduction of administrative fines under the PDPO. Currently Hong Kong has no mandatory breach reporting and the PCPD lacks power to impose fines directly. Amendments are under active consideration by the government.
data.whyItMatters: If enacted, would require DocuSign to report data breaches involving Hong Kong personal data to PCPD. Administrative fines would increase enforcement risk significantly — the current regime relies on criminal prosecution which is rarely used.
data.complianceImplications: Prepare breach notification procedures for HK. Budget for potential administrative fine regime. Current voluntary breach notification to PCPD would become mandatory.
data.penalties: Proposed — administrative fines expected to be modeled on GDPR-style proportional penalties
data.regulator: Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD)

data.shortName: HK AI Governance Policy Statement
data.fullName: Hong Kong SAR Government Policy Statement on Responsible AI
data.summary: The government published a policy statement on responsible development and use of AI, emphasizing a pro-innovation, risk-based approach. HKMA issued specific guidance for AI in banking. The government is monitoring international developments and considering whether sector-specific regulations are needed.
data.whyItMatters: Hong Kong's approach is currently light-touch and pro-innovation, but sector-specific regulations (particularly for financial services) may affect DocuSign's AI features used by HK financial institutions.
data.complianceImplications: Monitor sector-specific AI guidance, particularly from HKMA and SFC. Align AI features with responsible AI principles for financial services use cases.
data.penalties: No direct penalties — policy guidance. Sectoral regulators may impose requirements on regulated entities.
data.regulator: OGCIO / Innovation, Technology and Industry Bureau

data.shortName: NZ Modern Slavery Act (Proposed)
data.fullName: Modern Slavery and Worker Exploitation — Proposed Legislation
data.summary: New Zealand is considering modern slavery legislation following Australia and the UK. Proposed measures include mandatory supply chain transparency reporting for large entities, due diligence obligations, and a public register. Multiple advocacy groups and parliamentary inquiries have recommended legislation.
data.whyItMatters: If enacted, would create supply chain reporting obligations similar to Australia's Modern Slavery Act. DocuSign would likely be in scope as a large company operating in NZ.
data.complianceImplications: Monitor legislative developments. If enacted, prepare supply chain due diligence and annual reporting similar to AU Modern Slavery Act compliance.
data.penalties: TBD — expected to include financial penalties unlike Australia's current regime
data.regulator: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)

data.shortName: NZ Privacy Act Review — Enforcement Powers
data.fullName: Privacy Act 2020 — Review of Enforcement and Penalties Regime
data.summary: The Privacy Commissioner has called for strengthened enforcement powers including the ability to impose administrative fines and issue binding orders. Currently the Privacy Commissioner's enforcement tools are limited to compliance notices and naming. The government is reviewing whether GDPR-style administrative fines should be introduced.
data.whyItMatters: If administrative fines are introduced, NZ privacy compliance risk increases substantially. The current regime is relatively low-penalty compared to AU and SG — this would change the calculus.
data.complianceImplications: Monitor review progress. If fines are introduced, uplift NZ privacy compliance to match the increased enforcement risk.
data.penalties: Proposed — administrative fines under consideration

data.shortName: PH BSP Digital Banking Framework
data.fullName: BSP Circular 1105 — Digital Banking Framework and E-KYC
data.summary: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas framework for digital banking, including electronic know-your-customer (e-KYC) and electronic signature acceptance for financial transactions. Enables banks to onboard customers digitally and accept electronic signatures for account opening and loan agreements.
data.whyItMatters: Opens the Philippine banking sector to electronic signatures for customer onboarding and financial agreements. Direct market opportunity for DocuSign in financial services — one of the largest industries in the Philippines.
data.complianceImplications: Ensure e-signature workflows meet BSP requirements for financial transactions. Position DocuSign for banking e-KYC and digital onboarding use cases.
data.penalties: BSP supervisory enforcement for regulated financial institutions

data.shortName: PH Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Act (Proposed)
data.fullName: Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Act — Senate/House Bills
data.summary: Multiple bills filed to establish a legal framework for protecting critical information infrastructure in the Philippines. Would designate critical sectors, require cybersecurity standards, mandatory incident reporting, and regular security audits for CII operators and their service providers.
data.whyItMatters: If DocuSign provides services to designated critical infrastructure sectors in the Philippines (banking, government, telecommunications), it may face new cybersecurity compliance obligations as a service provider.
data.complianceImplications: Monitor bill progress. If enacted, assess whether DocuSign is a service provider to designated CII sectors. Prepare for potential incident reporting and security audit requirements.
data.penalties: TBD — bills propose imprisonment and fines for non-compliance with security standards
data.regulator: Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)

data.shortName: PH NPC Circular 2023-06 — Cross-Border Data Transfer
data.fullName: NPC Circular 2023-06 — Rules on Cross-Border Transfer of Personal Data
data.summary: National Privacy Commission circular establishing rules for cross-border transfers of Filipino personal data. Requires data controllers to conduct assessments before transferring personal data outside the Philippines, ensure adequate protection in receiving countries, and implement contractual safeguards.
data.whyItMatters: DocuSign processes Filipino personal data on infrastructure likely outside the Philippines. Cross-border transfer rules require documented assessments and safeguards for every transfer — directly affects DocuSign's data architecture.
data.complianceImplications: Conduct cross-border transfer assessments. Implement contractual safeguards (standard contractual clauses or equivalent). Document adequacy of protection in receiving jurisdictions. Maintain records of all cross-border transfers.
data.penalties: Data Privacy Act penalties apply — up to PHP 5 million and 6 years imprisonment
